title: Submagic Pricing: Plans, Costs and Limits (2026)
summary: Submagic pricing includes free and paid plans with different monthly video limits. Review each option's features and costs to select the right plan.
body_markdown:
## Submagic Plans, Prices and Limits Compared


### The direct answer


Submagic prices its three plans, Starter, Pro and Business, by how many videos you export and how long each one runs, meaning you need to estimate your usage to find the right plan, much as you would when sizing up any workflow you might later automate with a tool like[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) .


The monthly figure alone won't tell you your bill.


Submagic pricing is the tiered subscription structure, split into Starter, Pro and Business plans, under which the AI video-captioning tool charges according to how many videos you export each month and how long each one runs, rather than by a flat monthly fee.


Submagic is the AI captions and short-video editor. **Count your videos and caption minutes first, then pick the plan that covers them.**


**If you skip that count, you pay twice** : once for a plan too small, when exports run out mid-month, and again for the upgrade you make in a hurry.


### Every plan in one table


I couldn't confirm Submagic's current monthly price, annual price or video allowance. Nor could I confirm the maximum video length or export resolution for each plan as of 2026-11-12.


> If you skip that count, you pay twice: once for a plan too small, when exports run out mid-month, and again for the upgrade you make in a hurry.


If I put guessed numbers in a table, you'd budget against them, and that would be worse than no table.


Trust only the vendor's own page, submagic.co/pricing. When you open it, write down five things for each of the three plans:


1. The monthly price per member.
2. The annual price per member, which is usually a lower rate billed up front.
3. The number of videos you can export each month.
4. The longest single video the plan accepts.
5. The highest export resolution it allows.


Then multiply the per-member price by the number of people who will actually edit. A team of three pays three times the listed figure, and that's the line people tend to miss.


### What the credits, minutes and export limits count


You hit one limit first, and that one decides your plan. Two do most of the work: how many videos you export and how long each can be.


A creator posting short clips rarely hits the length cap, but a long interview cut into integrations can hit it on the first upload.


Fix a typo in a caption and export again, and that second export may count against your monthly allowance like a new video. That is **the quiet cost of re-exports** .


Activepieces charges 1 credit per flow run however many steps the flow holds, whereas Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so a ten-step hand-off around your exports costs the same as a two-step one.


Submagic's meter is the export, so check how its pricing page defines one before you assume a retry is free.
